description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

In this section (maximum 1000 words), please provide a global overview of the project progress **per output**. To what extent have they been achieved? Comment on the activities that have taken place and the most important milestones.

actual.value:
The project aimed to achieve one main output namely: Output 1: Arusha Technical College Solar Training Center (ATCSTC),and 5 other TVETS in Renewable Energy strengthened their research and education capacity, gender inclusiveness & sustainability.
Progress: This output was achieved fully, except for the development of online modules at ACT. This idea was not adopted as students are not able to do online learning on solar maintenance and report. In stead, we focus on accreditation and licensing of the solar services, which was essential and successful. We also focused a lot on generating publicity for the ACT, to increase enrollment. We co-created videos, brochures and ads, which wer widely spread. This has benefited both TAREA (new members) and the ACT College (though enrollment nrs were not yet available at the time of this report)> Below are key indicators and their achievements:
1. % alumni satisfied with the training and follow-up provided by MDF (at least 8/10 score) = 95% 2. % alumni (20 teachers) have gained useful skills that can be used when designing new training modules = 100% 3. % alumni (5 teachers) reporting to be inspired by study visit indicating commitment to improve solar education = 100% 4. # of new training modules or short courses developed and implemented with solar teachers for better connection to labour market and (self)employment. The revision of ATC Solar Centre is underway (see the report as attached). 5. # of online modules for short courses developed implemented = replaced by accreditation and licensing 6. % of renewable energy students satisfied with new modules = Revision is still underway. 7. Financial resource mobilization strategy / plan available for ACTSTC = 1 was developed and some NGOs already applied and received new grants. 8. # of actions implemented to improve access by female students gender equality = 3 actions (Awareness raising on gender beliefs, for example on how early marriage or FGM impacts, e.g. by NGOs; share opportunities on capacity building of individuals equally; support programs on capacity building for women).
Key activities that were undertaken to achieve this output included:
- Visit to the Strathmore University Solar Centre (5 ATC/TAREA Staff); - Research and Labour Market Surveys Training in Arusha - Curriculum development and delivery training in Arusha - Resource Mobilization and Gender Mainstreaming training in Arusha - Accreditation and Licensing and services delivery training in Arusha - Accreditation and review of ATC Solar Centre courses workshop in Moshi - Development and dissemination of the TAREA promotion and marketing video - Development and dissemination of the TAREA products and services brochures
